costDrivers.label: Jurisdictional Filming Permits and Municipal Filing Fees
costDrivers.reason: Filming permits in New Mexico are administered at the local city, town, or county level rather than by the state film office. Small production application fees and daily permit rates vary by jurisdiction (e.g., Santa Fe standard $25-$100 application fee plus $10/day shooting fee), alongside potential municipal processing costs.

costDrivers.label: General Liability and Production Insurance Coverage
costDrivers.reason: New Mexico jurisdictions and public property entities require comprehensive general liability insurance with standard coverage minimums of at least $1,000,000 to $1,050,000 to authorize filming activities.

costDrivers.label: Cast, Crew Labor, and Payroll Taxes/Fringes
costDrivers.reason: Production encompasses a 1-day shoot with 2 principal cast members (Mara and Jo) across 3 dialogue/rehearsal scenes. In New Mexico, standard payroll burden typically adds 24% to 28% on gross wages covering statutory insurance, workers' compensation (approx. 3.99%), and taxes, in addition to base day rates for cast and essential production crew.

costDrivers.label: State Refundable Film Production Tax Credit
costDrivers.reason: New Mexico offers a refundable film tax credit with a 25% base rate on qualified in-state spend and no minimum spend requirement, which can offset eligible post-production or production costs upon audit payout, though timing usually lags 6 to 18 months.

assumptions: Production schedule is set for a single 10-hour day (9.5 planned production hours) covering Scenes 1, 2, and 3.
Community Hall and Courtyard are co-located at a single facility or property, minimizing company moves and location rental fees.
Mara and Jo are non-minor performers; standard adult working hour guidelines and daily rest periods apply.

The low estimate reflects a micro-budget indie footprint with skeleton crew and standard equipment packages; the high estimate accounts for standard union/guild day rates, professional grip/electric packages, and contingency allowances.

locations.name: Santa Fe Community Center & Courtyard Facility
locations.fit: Accommodates both the interior community hall rehearsal scenes (Scene 1 and Scene 3) and the contiguous exterior courtyard rehearsal (Scene 2), allowing efficient movement between spaces during the single scheduled shoot day without company relocation.
risks: Permits are required for filming on both public and private property through the Santa Fe Film Office and are not guaranteed until formal application approval.
Exterior courtyard filming is vulnerable to ambient weather and variable natural lighting conditions during daytime shooting.
Production requires proof of comprehensive general liability insurance meeting New Mexico standards ($1,050,000 policy limit).

locations.name: Las Cruces Multipurpose Hall & Exterior Grounds
locations.fit: Provides a paired interior multipurpose hall and adjoining outdoor plaza/courtyard setup suitable for rehearsing duets and transitioning props between interior and exterior settings in southern New Mexico.
risks: Permit coordination must be arranged locally through Film Las Cruces, with mandatory 48-hour advance neighbor notifications within a 200-foot radius.
Facility access and operational booking dates remain unconfirmed and subject to municipal or private property owner availability.
Outdoor sound recording in the courtyard may be impacted by surrounding municipal traffic or environmental noise.

research.title: New Mexico Film Tax Incentives 2026: Credit, Rates & Caps - Shamel Studio
research.excerpt: The deep vendor network and experienced crew base mean that most department-head positions can be filled locally, reducing travel costs. ## New Mexico film incentive, _at a glance._ The questions producers ask first when sizing a New Mexicoshoot, answered against the state's current program structure and fringe environment. Is the New Mexico film tax credit refundable or transferable? New Mexico's film tax credit is refundable, meaning the state pays out the credit as cash regardless of the production company's in-state tax liability. Payouts typically arrive 6 to 18 months after a final certified audit. What is the New Mexico film incentive rate? New Mexico's base rate is 25% on qualified production spend, with stackable uplifts that can push the effective top rate to 40% (+10% rural (60+ mi from ABQ/Santa Fe); +5% TV pilot/series; +5% qualified facility). What is the minimum spend to qualify for the New Mexico film incentive? The minimum qualified-spend threshold to access the New Mexico program is None. Productions below this threshold are not eligible for the incentive. What is the annual cap on the New Mexico film tax credit? New Mexico's annual program cap is $140M (FY2026). Productions should confirm current fund availability before committing, as caps can be exhausted mid-fiscal-year. What is the payroll burden for film production in New Mexico? Typical payroll burden in New Mexico runs 24–28% on top of gross wages, covering payroll taxes, statutory insurance, and applicable union pension/health/welfare contributions. Workers' compensation rates for production work generally fall around 3.99%, and production purchases are subject to 5.125% GRT. Compare Across States ## See how New Mexico stacks up _on the full map._ Headline rate is the start, not the end. research.title: Nonresident Below-the-Line-Crew Credit… | New Mexico Film Office
research.excerpt: Skip To Content ### Choose New Mexico Section 7-2F-15 NMSA 1978 ### **The Refundable Film Production Tax Credit promotes and encourages hiring residents of New Mexico.** However, nonresident crew employed by a production can qualify for a 15% credit of the production’s total New Mexico budget for below-the-line crew wages and as determined by the New Mexico Film Office (NMFO), or up to 20% of the production’s total New Mexico budget for below-the-line-crew wages, specific requirements outlined below. Productions that are interested in participating in this credit will receive a 15% credit allowed for the payment of wages for below-the-line (BTL) crew who are **not** New Mexico residents. Services must be rendered in New Mexico and the film production company must make financial or promotional contributions toward educational or workforce development efforts in New Mexico as determined by the division. Please review the NM Taxation and Revenue [FYI-370 document](https://www.tax. ... 5% of the total nonresident below-the-line crew direct production expenditures (“direct production expenditures for the payment of wages, fringe benefits and per diem for nonresident industry crew made by the film production company to nonresident industry crew”). Productions will use the estimated NRCE credit max amount to calculate the giveback amount. The calculation can be found on page 13 of the FYI-370. The [NRCE / GIVEBACK SPREADSHEET](https://nmfilm.com/assets/uploads/NMFO-NRCE-Spreadsheet-2022.xlsx) provides an example of how to tally the giveback amount for NMFO’s review. **Please also send NMFO an excel list of the non-resident crew hired for review.** ** ** [List of approved giveback options](https://nmfilm.com/assets/uploads/Giveback-form-with-new-logo-2022.pdf) Alternative giveback options must be emailed to NMFO and pre-approved prior to the event/events taking place. Approved alternative giveback options must be coordinated and promoted with NMFO. Content must include mention of NMFO and NMFO incentives, positive feedback of filming in NM, film crew, locations, etc. If pre-approval from NMFO is not in writing the alternative giveback option will not be approved. Please email [nm.film@nmfilm.com](mailto:nm.film@nmfilm.com) with giveback questions.
